items.title: Jordan Says Its Deadly Strikes in Syria Targeted Islamic State
items.summary: The airstrikes late Monday, which a Syrian agency said killed at least seven civilians, were in retaliation for an attack on a Jordanian church, Jordan said.
items.full_text:
Title: Jordan Says Its Deadly Strikes in Syria Targeted Islamic State - The New York Times

URL Source: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/27/world/middleeast/jordan-syria-strikes-attack.html

Published Time: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 15:07:14 GMT

Markdown Content:
Jordan said on Tuesday that it had carried out deadly airstrikes on Islamic State targets in southern Syria a day earlier, an attack that killed at least seven civilians, including three children, according to the Syrian civil defense rescue service.

The Jordanian military, in a statement late Monday, said it was “targeting hide-outs of terrorist organizations” in retaliation for an [attack](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/23/world/middleeast/jordan-church-shooting.html) on a Greek Orthodox church in southern Jordan on Friday, which killed nine people.

The military did not identify the groups it had targeted, but a government spokesman, Mohammad al-Momani, said on Tuesday it was the Islamic State. He said the airstrikes had killed more than 20 operatives affiliated with the terror group, and that they were based on field intelligence about threats and plots against Jordan.

The Jordanian military said it coordinated the operation with the Syrian government, but the Syrian government gave a different version of events, saying the strikes on its territory came without prior coordination or notification. Mr. al-Momani did not address the issue in his statement, but he expressed the Jordanian government’s regret over civilian casualties.

Jordanian military jets struck Syria on the same day that Jordan’s security forces [arrested](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/26/world/middleeast/jordan-arrests-terror-attack-church.html) three men in Jordan who the authorities say are linked to the church attack, according to state media.

On Friday, gunmen emerged from a vehicle and opened fire on the church, in the village of Hamoud, during a funeral. In addition to the deaths, the attack left nearly three dozen people wounded.

Jordanian officials had previously said the deadly shooting was carried out by “terrorists,” but the statement on Tuesday was the first time the government had said the Islamic State was responsible.

The Islamic State still has cells inside Syria, despite having lost its last territorial foothold in the country in 2019, and it continues to carry out sporadic attacks. Last year, Syria joined the Global Coalition to Defeat the Islamic State, a U.S.-led effort to combat the group around the world.

In a statement on Tuesday, the Syrian government stopped short of condemning the strikes, saying it had launched an investigation. The government also said it stood in solidarity with the families of those killed and injured and would work to give them the necessary support.

“Concurrently, communication channels have been opened with our brothers in the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan to discuss the situation,” the statement said. “We underscore the importance of joint field and security coordination regarding any actions in the border regions, in a manner that preserves the sovereignty of the Syrian Arab Republic and safeguards the security and stability of both brotherly nations.”

Syria’s Foreign Ministry condemned the strikes in a statement on Tuesday, saying they were unacceptable incursions into Syrian airspace and constituted a violation of the country’s sovereignty. It said it was coordinating with Jordan to prevent further violations and secure their shared border.

In response to the strikes, Syria’s port authority announced the closure of the Nasib border crossing between southern Syria and Jordan starting on Tuesday “due to prevailing circumstances,” suspending passenger and commercial traffic in both directions.

Diplomatic relations between Syria and Jordan have warmed since the ouster of the Assad regime in Syria in late 2024.

The Jordanian strikes came days after Syria’s foreign minister, Asaad al-Shaibani, met with King Abdullah II of Jordan and other high-level officials to discuss the development of relations between the two countries and coordination on regional developments, including in southern Syria, according to Syrian state media.

Earlier, King Abdullah affirmed his country’s support for preserving Syria’s security and territorial integrity, in light of increasing Israeli attacks and incursions into southern Syria.

Jordanian officials have not said exactly what motivated the shooting at the church, one of the deadliest attacks in Jordan in years, which targeted the country’s small Christian minority. But hours after the attack, Prime Minister Jafar Hassan said that it was “the result of terrorist takfiri ideology,” an Arabic term commonly used to describe Islamist extremists who declare other Muslims heretics.

items.title: Meghan, Actress Turned Duchess, Will Join Australian Cooking Show
items.summary: The Duchess of Sussex will be a “special guest” next year on “Junior MasterChef Australia,” the channel that airs it announced.
items.full_text:
Title: Meghan, Actress Turned Duchess, Will Join Australian Cooking Show - The New York Times

URL Source: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/27/world/europe/meghan-junior-masterchef-australia.html

Published Time: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 15:28:04 GMT

Markdown Content:
Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, is pivoting again, this time to Australian reality TV.

Meghan, an American actress who became part of the British royal family when she married Prince Harry in 2018, will be a “special guest” next year on “Junior MasterChef Australia,” according to Channel 10, which airs the show, Australia’s version of the popular cooking competition.

The channel said that [a guest appearance by the duchess](https://www.nine.com.au/lifestyle/royals/meghan-markle-masterchef-australia-guest-judge-20260723-p60hqm.html) earlier this year on “MasterChef Australia,” the adult version of the competition, drew “the program’s largest Sunday audience since 2023.” Meghan, whose office released the same statement as was issued by Channel 10, said she had had an “incredible time” on the show.

“So when they approached me to come back and work with this young group of talent, it was an easy yes,” she said in the statement.

Since Meghan and Harry, the Duchess and Duke of Sussex, [moved back to Britain](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/20/world/europe/prince-harry-meghan-uk-move-return.html?eafs_enabled=false) from the United States earlier this year, there has been much speculation about their next moves. The two [left Britain in 2020](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/19/world/europe/harry-meghan-uk-royals-timeline.html) in a public break with the royal family, giving up their loftiest titles and stepping away from their royal duties.

Over six years in California, the [couple’s star power faded](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/22/us/meghan-harry-hollywood-uk-move.html). Netflix chose not to renew a multimillion-dollar deal with them, and an arrangement with the audio platform Spotify fell short of expectations.

For Harry, returning to Britain meant [a return to the charities](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/20/world/europe/harry-meghan-britain-return.html) that he had spent much of his life representing. For the couple’s children, Archie, 7 and Lilibet, 5, it has meant growing up in the homeland of their [royal family](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/22/world/europe/harry-meghan-children-schools.html). It was less clear what Meghan would do, though it was briefly rumored that she would join the cast of Guy Ritchie’s Netflix crime series “The Gentlemen.”

Even as a working royal, Meghan tried to maintain an independent career as an actress and a lifestyle entrepreneur. Though Netflix canceled “[With Love, Meghan](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/04/02/dining/meghan-markle-kitchen-as-ever.html),” a show in which she presented herself as a domestic goddess in the mold of Martha Stewart, her product line “As Ever,” featuring items like raspberry jam and dried flower petals, is [said to remain lucrative](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/08/22/style/meghan-markle-as-ever.html).

Meghan is no stranger to a TV kitchen. In 2016, before marrying Harry, she was a guest judge on “Chopped Junior,” a children’s cooking show on the Food Network in the United States.

“I love cooking with my own kids, so seeing what these young stars create in the kitchen is going to be a lot of fun,” Meghan said in the Tuesday statement.

items.title: China Steps In to Rescue Stocks, But the Market Continues to Fall
items.summary: The Communist Party uses a “national team” of state-owned investment funds to stem the market rout. But this time, investors are not sure it will work.
items.full_text:
Title: China Steps In to Rescue Stocks, But the Market Continues to Fall - The New York Times

URL Source: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/27/business/china-stocks-losses-government-intervention.html

Published Time: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 15:30:06 GMT

Markdown Content:
As investor pessimism pushed China’s stock market into a bear market last week, officials responded as they often do, deploying a group of state-owned funds to arrest the slide.

The group of Beijing-backed investment companies, known colloquially as the “national team,” pumped $6.8 billion into stocks in a single session last Thursday, providing a temporary reprieve to a market that had fallen for 11 straight weeks.

Mainland stocks are down more than 20 percent from a recent peak — the threshold for a bear market.

But this time, investors are signaling that the old playbook may not be enough. By Tuesday, markets fell again, declining 1.3 percent. Stocks in China are among the worst performers in Asia this year, along with Indonesia and India.

The intervention may have helped to “prop up the market,” [said](https://m.weibo.cn/status/5357492067895033) Shi Shusi, a financial commentator with 2.6 million followers on Chinese social media. But, he added, “it couldn’t prop up investors’ confidence.”

The effort to stabilize stocks came just days before Xi Jinping, China’s leader, convened one of the country’s most important political meetings of the year. Hundreds of the [Communist Party’s most senior officials](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/26/world/asia/china-communist-party-xi-forever-purge.html) are meeting to set the government agenda. While economic policy has traditionally been a priority at such gatherings, many observers expect it to take a back seat to politics this year.

The market sell-off reflects a deeper unease about China’s economy and growing doubts about whether policymakers are doing enough to turn things around. China’s manufacturing juggernaut has powered a [surge in exports](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/18/business/china-economy-gdp.html), sustaining economic growth and helping Beijing meet its targets.

But that strength has obscured persistent weakness at home.

Wage growth is slowing. Companies are struggling to raise prices. And households, whose savings are largely tied up in real estate, continue to see their wealth eroded by falling home prices.

Image

The skyline of the Lujiazui financial district in Shanghai. Chinese officials have focused on reassuring markets, but investors are hoping for more action.Credit...Qilai Shen for The New York Times

“If the government keeps pumping money in, we will see short-term gains, but this will not continue,” said Gary Ng, a senior economist for Asia Pacific with Natixis Corporate & Investment Banking, referring to the national team, which also intervened in July to steady the market.

“The government will try to set a floor here, but whether there could be a strong momentum for rebound will take a lot more than what we see right now,” he added.

For many investors, the bigger concern is that Mr. Xi seems more focused on his political aims than on stimulating growth. That priority is on display this week as officials meet to lay the groundwork for his fourth term as party leader.

Beijing has intensified an anti-corruption campaign that ensnares around one million officials each year. Under Mr. Xi, China has tightened scrutiny of money flowing overseas and stepped up regulatory and antitrust actions against prominent companies.

Those measures have unnerved entrepreneurs, analysts said, adding to uncertainty about the business environment.

Local governments have also pulled back subsidies and tax breaks, making companies more cautious about investing.

Some of the sharpest declines in recent weeks have come from artificial intelligence companies, once among the market’s biggest sources of optimism.

Shares of Cambricon Technologies, a state-backed chipmaker seen as a Chinese rival to Nvidia, have fallen more than 10 percent over the past month. The CSI Artificial Intelligence Index, which tracks leading Chinese A.I. companies, has dropped 19 percent over the same period.

Investors are now searching for signs that Beijing will go beyond buying stocks and introduce broader measures to revive the economy.

“We’re reaching the pain point where officials feel they must intervene,” said Christopher Beddor, deputy director of China research at Gavekal Dragonomics.

In 2024, China’s central bank unveiled a sweeping package of measures to bolster confidence and stimulate growth. It cut short-term interest rates and freed up state-controlled banks to lend more. At a rare news conference, the central bank governor signaled that it could provide further support.

Stocks [surged](https://www.nytimes.com/2024/09/27/business/asia-stocks-csi-300.html), posting their biggest gains since the 2008 financial crisis.

Image

Wu Qing, chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, has sought to reassure investors that the government was safeguarding the markets.Credit...Vincent Thian/Associated Press

But analysts are skeptical that policymakers will adopt the same approach this time. Even large purchases by the national team are no substitute for the wide-ranging stimulus investors have long hoped for.

Instead, Chinese officials have focused on reassuring markets.

Speaking at a forum last week, Wu Qing, chairman of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, told investors that market steadiness remained a priority. The government was “making every effort to safeguard the security and stability of the capital market,” he [said](https://www.csrc.gov.cn/csrc/c106311/c7665578/content.shtml).

State media have amplified the message.

On the same day, China’s state broadcaster [declared](https://baijiahao.baidu.com/s?id=1879656176340824850&wfr=spider&for=pc) that “positive signs are increasing,” and that “the basis for market resilience remains firmly in place.”

The People’s Daily, the Communist Party’s official newspaper, also struck [an upbeat tone](https://paper.people.com.cn/rmrb/pc/content/202610/26/content_30187536.html) this week, pointing to China’s “reasonable” economic growth despite geopolitical conflicts and a fragile global economy.

Emphasizing the importance of “high-quality development,” the article described growth as a “long-term endeavor,” warning that “winds and rains are inevitable along the way.”
